source: (That's everyone, I think. I'll have to let Irma know when she's next avaliable.)
This card game you mentioned -- it's unpopular with the others?
Correct, Fräulein!
Once they come to see it as I do, though, I'm certain they'll throw aside Runfa and Triomphe and see the light!
That old man Marcellus is asking for another defeat...
And my fingers itch for a gamble if I go without too long!
Irma has asked me to invite you to a game of Ruff and Honors.
Oh, music to my ears! We've been playing that awful Italian one... Runfa.
I introduced it to the men, and they won't stop clinging to it. I've told them it's a dreadful game.
Well, I suppose I have to gather every penny I own so I can lose it all to her!
Wait—I haven't got a cent. That's right.
You... don't have any money?
When one is an expert in the art of acquiring free meals, one wants for very little in this world, my dear girl.
Irma has requested your presence at a card game. Ruff and Honors, I believe.
Wah hah hah! Time for a rematch...
If she breaks out the trick deck again, I'll wring 'er neck, though!
Brit asked me to facilitate a 'rendezvous' between herself and Hamlet.
You're certain?
Well, yes. She made the request directly to me. As a favor.
That's not good.
A while ago, she told me her father told her he was beginning to take the the thought of a betrothal more seriously.
With Hamlet as the most likely suitor.
Quite a love match, that one.
I... I just spoke with her. I thought... we were...
Oh my god. She's going to wind up marrying him. I never had a real chance, did I?
I feel ill. I need to see her. To speak with her.
This can't happen.
So—you want to meet with Hamlet tonight?
Yes, that is the precise thing we talked about already. Sharp as a spoon, you are!
We're going to have a lovely private little evening, he and I.
Lady Brit has asked me to facilitate a... meeting between the two of you.
A private meeting?
I think she wanted to ask you on a date, of sorts.
I cannot bear to think of seeing her again before I must meet her at the altar, now that we are to be wed.
I've no interest in going, but thank you for letting me know.
Hm. I've little interest in that, whatever she might be scheming.
She asked you this?
Can she not be direct with her invitation?
I ask myself the same question. Trust me.
Making you her hound... I thought you above that.
Well, color me intrigued. If she wants to meet by moonlight, then let's meet.
(Well, that's done. For better or worse. I'll have to let Brit know when I can.)
Lady Brit has asked me to facilitate a meeting between herself and Hamlet.
This should be good news, is it not?
It means he's moved on to some poor new girl!
I always got the impression he didn't like her very much.
One is not always privy to the inner machinations of another's heart, dearest.
Anyway, enough waxing philosophical. The viper is out of your grass. For good.
My lady, Brit and the Prince intend to meet late tonight for a... 'rendezvous'.
Well, well!
How did you hear about this, Ophelia?
From the lady Brit herself.
She's exploiting him at a particularly dark moment.
My son is going through so much right now. As are you. For Brit to make this request of you, and of him...
It's horrid.
I'll write to her father at once. Such behavior is incredibly unbecoming of a lady of the court.
Well. If it's a party of two, I'm sure Hamlet won't mind if his dear mother joins him.
I love moonlight walks! Almost as much as I love my dearest lady-in-waiting exploiting my son's weakened emotional state.
I'll meet them tonight. As you were, Ophelia.
Did you know the Queen was having an affair with King Claudius before her husband's death?
It matters not. Now all the others do, too.
Where did you hear that?
Her journal. I found it myself.
I see. Yes, I knew. But I would choose to keep any of my lady's secrets a hundred times over.
Gerta died in such pain, alone.
Always be kind to those whose actions you disapprove of, Ophelia. Someday, you may be them.
And then you will wish someone had granted you mercy in return.
Please, do not hurt Gerta further. It would devastate her. And she suffers so deeply now.
My lord, I know that the Queen was having an affair with you before her husband's death.
But tell me, does that matter now?
Neither he nor she live. That part of my life is truly gone. There's nothing left to talk about.
Of course. I see. Then let's not speak of it any more.
Speak to me of it no more.
My nephew's punishment was a fitting fate for such an insidious rumor.
Do you have any idea how distressed she is? She won't even look at me.
And she... my beautiful wife... she holds a place at God's side. I know it.
She was twice the human as I. And she died in shame, alone, afraid.
There will be no peace for me until I, too, rest with her.
Are you implying my wife—your queen—is a harlot?
Be silent, lest I break you! Whoever told you this will pay with their life!
I know that Queen Gertrude was having an affair with Claudius before King Hamlet's death.
Yes. Well, everyone does, now.
Quite cruel of Hamlet to announce it so publicly, but admittedly I'm stunned at her indiscretion.
King Hamlet loved her with the fondness of ten men. And she betrayed him.
I suppose we all harbor our dark secrets.
Ophelia, what are you thinking? You can't be spreading rumors like that!
It's not a rumor.
I've tried to tell you before what a delicate situation we're in, dearheart.
Please don't do anything to bring shame upon us.
Hamlet, I have reason to believe your mother had an affair with your uncle before your father's death.
I found the diary of hers you requested. Everything's in there.
I came across... a diary of hers. She wrote about it, extensively.
And now she's dead.
I... never... knew.
I wonder what else Mother took to the grave, held close.
Frailty, thy name is woman.
My father would have done anything for my mother.
Claudius was a satyr next to his Hyperion, Ophelia.
My father desired such a gentle world for her that he would have kept the winds of heaven from visiting her face too roughly.
Before the slippers she wore to his funeral had even been broken in-- a funeral where she followed his body like Niobe, all tears--
She was already marrying him. My uncle! Such dexterity to incestuous sheets.
Nothing about this is good, and it must never come to good.
She should suffer for what she's done.
Hamlet, be reasonable...
Ophelia, do you believe... in spirits?
Listen. When I ran into your bedchamber earlier, I wasn't mad. I swear it.
I saw my father's spirit on the castle walls. It spoke to me.
Your father's ghost?
I... saw the spirit in a dream, too, I think...
My father's spirit claimed he had been murdered.
He told me that my mother was unfaithful to him when he still lived.
And if we now know that's true, it must be true as well that my uncle killed my father and covered up his crime.
Claudius... is a killer. This, I already knew.
Were my mother to tell me now that she never suspected him, I wouldn't believe her for an instant.
I was planning to just kill him, but knowing the both of them are equally complicit...
I've something special in mind for the both of them, now.
Please, think carefully...
The time for that has passed. Now I want only revenge for my father.
On her, and him.
Tomorrow I'll make my move, when everyone is next gathered...
You must be there, Ophelia. You must bear witness to all this. Then I'll take you to meet Father's spirit, and you'll understand why it had to be this way.
Today I'll make my move, when everyone is next gathered...
It's too late for me to do something public about this-- expose them for who they are, on stage...
But they will all face justice soon enough. It seems inevitable, now.
(This... won't end well.)
I know, my lady, that you were with Claudius before your husband's death.
I suppose the worst has happened, now. And they all know.
I have nothing with which to defend myself. Let them hate me, however they will.
It has been a miserable life in many ways, this one.
And there it is. Someone knows.
I don't know how you know. But it doesn't matter, in the end.
I had expected that one day someone I love would approach me and say this very thing.
But perhaps I had thought it might be some distant day. Not now.
I suppose the worst will soon happen. If you know, then the others soon shall.
If there is any love in your heart, you will not unveil me to them, Ophelia. I beg this of you. Please.
I've found proof that the Queen was dishonest with her husband before his death, and loved King Claudius.
Oh, my! That sounds like precisely the sort of thing that'll get your head lopped off.
Do run and tell the others, won't you? It's gotten a bit dull around here.
Quince, I have proof that King Claudius is a murderer. He killed his own brother.
Proof, have we?
I heard him confess. And I think he's going to come after Hamlet next.
Mmm. And what are you going to do about it?
You already know how this particular move can play out, after all.
But—perhaps—there's a way to use this information differently. Something I haven't found.
Oh, my. You still think I'm going to help you. That's rather cute.
Get lost, darling.
I... don't know. King Hamlet's spirit seems to want revenge...
I told Hamlet. He was upset, horrified. He asked me to find his mother's private diary.
He believed it would contain some confession to the crime.
What I found contained within was... less than savory, but not proof that Claudius killed anyone.
The way I see it, my dear, certain options lie before you.
You could find concrete proof of his actions. This, of course, would be kept in his most private of places.
Of course, a sufficiently motivated girl might take matters into her own hands and rid Elsinore of such a killer.
The most difficult option would be to remove the teeth from his best-laid plans, keeping a close eye on his bare-backed nephew.
Sent to England, wasn't he, that boy? Such a gruesome way to die.
And if he avoids that, there's that awful poisoned sword incident...
